decisions.decision: Phase 23 reframed from greenfield Phase-23-as-roadmapped to regression-fix scope
decisions.rationale: User clarification: 'we had a working CI pipeline that built cross platform targets... just want that back'. Captured in 23-CONTEXT.md (commit a07b1a4ish — earlier today)

decisions.decision: Bundle vendored ffmpeg trees in the repo (libs/ffmpeg/<platform>/) instead of rebuilding from source on every CI run
decisions.rationale: User question: 'whats so problematic with ffmpeg, can we just bundle it in our repo, would that help?'. Eliminates 15-25 min/CI from-source build, removes entire MSYS2 toolchain-rot surface. Cost: ~25 MB repo growth, manageable. Trees committed: macos-arm64 (a51bb04), macos-x86_64 (pre-existing), windows-x86_64 (50b7678). Linux next.

decisions.decision: MSVC .lib import libraries for Windows ffmpeg generated via gendef + dlltool post-process
decisions.rationale: ffmpeg's MinGW autotools build produces .dll.a MinGW-format import libs that MSVC's link.exe rejects. dlltool --output-lib emits COFF that MSVC accepts for ffmpeg's C symbols. Same pattern as the openh264 fix. Generated .lib files committed at libs/ffmpeg/windows-x86_64/lib/.

decisions.decision: Ship Windows beta unsigned (SmartScreen 'More info → Run anyway' on first launch)
decisions.rationale: Memory project_apple_signing documents only the Apple cert; no Windows code-signing cert exists. EV cert acquisition (~$300+/yr, slow procurement) deferred to v1.4 if SmartScreen friction becomes a real adoption blocker.

decisions.decision: macOS Universal stitching via lipo'd universal dylibs in CMAKE_BINARY_DIR/ffmpeg-universal/ (not committed to repo)
decisions.rationale: cmake/ffmpeg.cmake detects multi-arch CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES and lipos the per-arch macos-{arm64,x86_64} trees into universal dylibs at configure time. Build-tree only; regenerated on build dir wipe. Local Intel-only dev path uses libs/ffmpeg/macos-x86_64/ directly (no lipo).

decisions.decision: CI scope: local stays Intel-only fast iteration, CI is the place where cross-platform/universal happens
decisions.rationale: User directive: 'no need to build universal locally, just CI. local is only intel mac, much faster. but CI is the purpose to build cross platform'

decisions.rationale: User redirect: 'doesn't make sense to run this as a full phase, we need to debug in iterations about whats breaking'. CONTEXT.md still useful as the regression inventory + locked decisions; no PLAN.md was written.
